references.text: The prophet Malachi predicts that God will send his messenger to clear the way before him: "Behold, I send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me" (Mal 3:1). John the Baptist is the fulfillment of this prophecy as the one sent from God.
Isaiah prophesies about "a voice crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord" (Isa 40:3). John the Baptist is identified with this voice—a man sent by God to prepare the people.
Luke's account of how the angel Gabriel announces John's birth to Zechariah (Luk 1:13-17). Here it is confirmed that John was sent by God with a specific mission: to turn the people back to the Lord.

In Zechariah's song of praise, John is called "the prophet of the Most High" who shall "go before the Lord to prepare his ways" (Luk 1:76-77). This emphasizes that he was a man sent from God with a prophetic mission.
John the Baptist himself testifies about his mission and identifies himself as "the voice of one crying in the wilderness" (Joh 1:19-23). He is sent by God to bear witness to Christ.

John testifies that "he who sent me to baptize with water" gave him the sign of the Spirit descending upon the Messiah (Joh 1:33-34). The expression "he who sent me" confirms that John was sent by God.

Matthew's account of John the Baptist appearing in the wilderness of Judea (Matt 3:1-3) as the one fulfilling Isaiah's prophecy. He came with a message of repentance—sent by God to prepare the way for the Messiah.

Mark opens his gospel by quoting the prophecy about the messenger and identifies John the Baptist as its fulfillment (Mar 1:2-4). John came and "baptized in the wilderness and preached a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins."

John the Baptist reminds his disciples that "I am not the Christ, but I have been sent before him" (Joh 3:28). The words "sent before him" correspond to the expression "sent from God" in the prologue of John's Gospel.

Jesus himself quotes the prophecy about John: "Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who shall prepare your way" (Matt 11:10). This confirms that John the Baptist was a man sent by God with a specific mission.
